intro: When you search for income protection insurance near me, you're likely looking for someone local who can help you protect your income if illness or injury stops you working. You want to understand how this cover works and find a broker who can explain your options clearly. iComply introduces you to a UK insurance broker who can discuss your needs and provide a quote.
need_heading: What people searching for income protection insurance near me usually need
need_lead: Most people want to know how to protect their income and find a broker who can guide them through the process.
needs: You want to understand how income protection insurance works and whether it suits your circumstances.
You are self-employed and worried about what would happen to your income if you couldn't work due to illness or injury.
You have a mortgage or family commitments and need reassurance that your income would be replaced if the unexpected happens.
You are confused by policy terms like deferred periods and own-occupation definitions and want expert explanation.
You want to find a local broker who can compare policies and give you a personalised quote.
context: Income protection insurance replaces part of your income if illness or injury stops you working, until you return or the policy ends. Key features include the deferred period (how long you wait before payments start) and the definition of incapacity, with own-occupation definitions generally being the most comprehensive.

Brokers must be authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm. You can check them on the FCA register. Many brokers belong to the British Insurance Brokers' Association (BIBA), and some hold Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute. Brokers must understand your demands and needs, explain key policy features and exclusions, and tell you how they are paid.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when enquiring
tell: Your occupation and whether you are employed or self-employed, as this affects the type of cover available.
Your approximate annual income, so the broker can discuss suitable levels of cover.
Any existing health conditions or hobbies that might affect your policy.
Whether you have a mortgage or dependants relying on your income.
How long you could manage without income if you were unable to work, to help decide on a deferred period.
Any preferences you have for dealing with a local broker or a specific type of policy.
questions: What is the difference between own-occupation and any-occupation definitions, and which applies to your policy?
How does the deferred period affect the cost of the policy?
What exclusions might apply to my occupation or health situation?
How much of my income can be covered, and how is that calculated?
How are you paid for your services, and will I receive a clear explanation of fees?
What happens if I need to make a claim, and how does the claims process work?

faqs.q: Do I need income protection insurance if I am self-employed?
faqs.a: Income protection can be particularly valuable for self-employed people, as you may not have employer sick pay or other support if you cannot work. A broker can explain how cover works for your situation.

faqs.q: How is income protection insurance different from critical illness cover?
faqs.a: Income protection pays a regular income if you cannot work due to illness or injury, while critical illness cover pays a lump sum on diagnosis of a specified condition. A broker can help you understand the differences and decide what suits you.

faqs.q: Can I get income protection insurance if I have a pre-existing medical condition?
faqs.a: Insurers may offer cover with exclusions or at a higher premium, depending on the condition. A broker can approach insurers to find out what is available for you.

faqs.q: How do I check that a broker is authorised?
faqs.a: You can check on the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) register to see if a broker is authorised or an appointed representative. Many brokers also belong to the British Insurance Brokers' Association (BIBA).
